evals.prompt: I have a Node.js REST API that listens on port 3000 and exposes a /health endpoint. It needs to scale automatically based on CPU usage and should run with minimal privileges. Create a Helm chart for it with security hardening and HPA configured.
evals.expected_output: A complete Helm chart with Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, HPA, and hardened security context (non-root user, read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities)

assertions.text: Chart contains Deployment or StatefulSet resource
Chart includes HorizontalPodAutoscaler for scaling
Deployment includes hardened securityContext with non-root user
Container drops ALL Linux capabilities
Container uses read-only root filesystem
Chart includes RBAC resources (ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding)
Chart includes NetworkPolicy for traffic control
Deployment includes health check probes (livenessProbe/readinessProbe)
Chart includes Service resource
Chart includes values.yaml with configurable parameters

evals.prompt: I need to deploy a PostgreSQL database to Kubernetes. It needs persistent storage, should run as non-root, and must be able to accept connections from application pods in the same namespace. Create a Helm chart with a StatefulSet.
evals.expected_output: A StatefulSet-based Helm chart with PersistentVolumeClaim, headless Service, RBAC, hardened security, NetworkPolicy allowing connections from app pods

assertions.text: Chart uses StatefulSet for the database workload
StatefulSet includes volumeClaimTemplates for persistent storage
Chart includes headless Service (clusterIP: None) for DNS discovery
StatefulSet runs as non-root user
StatefulSet includes init container to handle permissions
Chart includes NetworkPolicy allowing same-namespace connections
Chart includes ServiceAccount for RBAC
StatefulSet includes health check probes

evals.prompt: I'm deploying a multi-container pod with an Nginx reverse proxy sidecar next to my Go application on port 8080. The app needs to write logs to /var/log/app and expose metrics on /metrics. Create a hardened Helm chart.
evals.expected_output: Deployment with two containers, shared emptyDir volume for logs with proper ownership, hardened security contexts for both containers, NetworkPolicy, health checks on metrics endpoint

assertions.text: Chart contains Deployment resource
Deployment includes multiple containers (main + sidecar)
Deployment includes shared emptyDir volume for logs
Pod security context includes fsGroup for volume ownership
Both containers have hardened security context
Chart includes ConfigMap for Nginx configuration
Deployment has health check probes
Chart includes NetworkPolicy

evals.prompt: I need a Helm chart for a backup job that runs every day at 2 AM. It connects to a database using a secret (connection string), reads a config file from a ConfigMap for backup options, and uploads to S3. Create a CronJob with proper security hardening.
evals.expected_output: A CronJob Helm chart with Secret and ConfigMap resources, hardened Pod template (non-root, read-only root, dropped caps), volumeMounts for secret and configmap, RBAC for service account, NetworkPolicy, proper restart policy

assertions.text: Chart contains CronJob resource
CronJob has a schedule defined (for daily 2 AM execution)
CronJob pod mounts Secret for database credentials
Chart includes ConfigMap for backup configuration
Chart includes Secret resource template
CronJob pod template has hardened security context (non-root)
CronJob containers drop capabilities
Chart includes ServiceAccount for CronJob RBAC
CronJob specifies restart policy

evals.prompt: I have a web application that needs database connection secrets (username, password, host) and a config file (database pool size, timeouts). Create a Helm chart that uses both Secrets and ConfigMaps, with the values parameterized so I can deploy to dev, staging, and prod.
evals.expected_output: Deployment Helm chart with Secret and ConfigMap templates, values.yaml with environment-specific parameters, hardened security context, proper volumeMounts for both secret and configmap, examples of different values for each environment

assertions.text: Chart contains Deployment resource
Chart includes Secret template for database credentials
Chart includes ConfigMap template for database configuration
Chart includes values-dev.yaml for development environment
Chart includes values-staging.yaml for staging environment
Chart includes values-prod.yaml for production environment
Deployment includes hardened security context
Deployment mounts Secret as volume
Deployment mounts ConfigMap as volume
Chart includes Service resource
